Re: Appeal of denial for knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy  
CPT 29881

Dear Appeals Reviewer:

I am appealing Harvard Pilgrim’s denial of prior authorization for CPT 29881, knee arthroscopy with meniscectomy. The denial dated August 9, 2026, states that the submitted documentation was incomplete and did not allow a determination of medical necessity.

The enclosed records address the medical necessity of the requested procedure:

- I have had 18 months of progressive knee pain that has not resolved with rest.
- I completed 20 supervised physical-therapy visits over 14 weeks, from March 26, 2026, through July 2, 2026. Therapy focused on quadriceps strengthening and range of motion, but symptoms persisted. The physical-therapy discharge note documents this course of treatment.
- I used NSAIDs for four months without adequate relief.
- A corticosteroid injection on May 13, 2026, produced only two weeks of partial relief.
- MRI performed on July 14, 2026, demonstrated a displaced bucket-handle tear of the medial meniscus with mechanical locking.
- I experience locking and giving way, cannot squat or kneel, and am limited to level walking.
- Examination showed positive provocative testing on the affected side, with range of motion limited by pain.
- The MRI showed preserved articular cartilage and Kellgren-Lawrence grade 1 changes, supporting that the principal structural problem is the displaced medial-meniscus tear rather than advanced arthritis.
- I have no active infection or untreated substance-use condition. My BMI is 29, and I am a nonsmoker.

These records document a symptomatic displaced meniscal tear with mechanical locking, persistent functional impairment, failed conservative treatment, objective MRI findings, and examination findings. They also provide the clinical history and risk information needed to evaluate the requested arthroscopy.

Please overturn the denial and authorize CPT 29881. If Harvard Pilgrim maintains the denial, please identify each specific item of information that remains missing and provide the exact clinical-review criteria and criteria version applied to this request, including the criteria used for CPT 29881. The publicly available information I located identifies the commercial review standard but does not publish the procedure-specific criteria, policy number, or effective date; therefore, I have not quoted or reconstructed any plan policy language in this appeal.

Please also provide the clinical rationale for any continued denial and explain how the enclosed records fail to satisfy the criteria applied.

The treating surgeon is Reyes, MD, orthopedic surgery. Please include the enclosed clinical records in the reconsideration of this request.

Sincerely,

Harper Delgado  
Member ID: W267205200  
[Telephone number]

[Email address]
